name: Sodium/potassium manipulation (peak week)

card.summary: Bodybuilder-style salt and water adjustments before a show or shoot; documented as part of contest prep, with associated health risks.
card.note: Dehydration and electrolyte shifts have documented health risks.

quick.overview:
Peak week is the final stretch of bodybuilding contest preparation, in which competitors adjust carbohydrate, water and electrolyte intake to look more defined on stage. Some appearance-focused people borrow the idea for photo shoots.

Available reference sources describe the general approach only briefly, and no controlled study of the sodium and potassium aspect was found.
quick.mechanism: Proponents say altering sodium, potassium and water intake changes how much fluid sits under the skin and in muscle. Carbohydrate loading in the final stage is described as refilling glycogen, which holds water.
quick.risks: Intentional dehydration is among practices linked in reference material to higher death rates among bodybuilders. Dehydration of even a few percent of body water can impair cognition and cause dizziness, and larger losses are dangerous.

lead: Sodium and potassium manipulation during peak week refers to deliberate changes to salt, potassium and fluid intake in the days before a bodybuilding contest or photo shoot, with the stated aim of a drier, more defined look. It is part of the final contest-prep stage, which reference sources describe as combining carbohydrate loading with dehydration [1].

The wiki found no controlled studies of the sodium or potassium protocols themselves. Reference material notes that intentional dehydration is among practices associated with elevated mortality among bodybuilders [1], and medical sources describe the effects of dehydration [2].
infobox: Final days before a show or shoot

paras: Competitors typically spend 12 to 14 weeks cutting, then in the final stage combine carbohydrate loading with dehydration to sharpen muscle definition and vascularity [1]. Sodium and potassium changes are one set of tactics within that final stage. Specific protocols are not described here.

Proponents say fluid distribution can be shifted by changing electrolyte and water intake. Glycogen is stored with water [3], and carbohydrate loading is documented to cause water retention [4]. Medical sources note that sodium retention drives swelling in some conditions and that kidneys regulate water and sodium [5].

Dehydration causes thirst, headache and fatigue, and a loss of 1 to 2 percent of body water can impair thinking; losses of 5 to 8 percent can cause fatigue and dizziness, and more severe losses can be fatal [2]. Reference material lists intentional dehydration among training practices linked to higher death rates in bodybuilders [1].

lore.intro: Peak-week tactics are discussed in physique communities and sometimes adapted by people seeking a sharper look for photos.

claims.claim: Manipulating salt and water makes you look drier and more defined.
claims.believers: Competitors say it improves definition and vascularity on stage.
claims.experts: Reference material describes dehydration and carbohydrate loading as part of contest prep [1]; no controlled study of appearance effects was found.

claims.claim: These methods are safe if done briefly.
claims.believers: Some users describe short protocols as low-risk.
claims.experts: Dehydration has documented effects on cognition and health [2], and intentional dehydration is linked with higher mortality in bodybuilders [1].
